title: Accelerating AI on Edge — Chintan Parikh and Weiyi Wang, Google DeepMind

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary object is LiteRT, an on-device inference runtime covering quantization, hardware acceleration, and latency/cost tradeoffs across edge platforms. LiteRT is a general-purpose edge inference framework serving developers building AI applications across multiple platforms. The talk addresses deploying and running trained models in production on edge devices at scale. Content assumes familiarity with ML deployment concepts but remains accessible to practitioners building edge AI systems. Conference presentation with live demos, benchmarks, and Q&A. Includes specific quantitative performance claims, live demonstrations, and stated production scale metrics.

summary: Chintan Parekh, product manager for LiteRT at Google AI Edge, presents on accelerating AI on edge devices, focusing on Gemma 4 Edge models (E2B and E4B). He begins by outlining edge benefits: latency for real-time use cases like camera filters and video calls, privacy for sensitive document summarization, offline capability for poor connectivity, and cost offsets through hybrid edge-cloud deployment. The Gemma 4E 2B model uses roughly 1-2 GB of RAM after quantization, suiting voice interfaces and summarization, while the 4B model targets heavier platforms like laptops and IoT devices. New agent capabilities include built-in function calling for local API interaction, native structured JSON output encoded in model architecture rather than prompt engineering, a chain-of-thought thinking mode, and hardware-native cross-platform support. Models are Apache 2.0 licensed and available on Hugging Face. Parekh demos a gallery app showcasing on-device agent skills: Wikipedia querying, mood and sleep tracking with reasoning, photo-to-music pairing, and animal vocal call sound generation. The app supports user-created skills, CPU/GPU/NPU acceleration selection, and is open source on GitHub. LiteRT, Google's on-device framework built on TensorFlow Lite, underpins these experiences with 100,000+ apps and billions of active users. LiteRT supports cross-platform deployment across Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, web, and IoT using the same TFLite model format. It accepts not just TensorFlow Lite models but also PyTorch and JAX models via conversion paths. The development stack includes LiteRT Torch for model conversion, a model explorer tool for graph inspection and mixed-precision quantization, and the AI Edge Portal, a cloud-based benchmarking service for testing deployability across device fleets. CPU and GPU acceleration are universally available, while NPU integration is complete with Qualcomm and MediaTek plus additional partner integrations underway, delivering 3-10x improvement for real-time AR/VR and TTS use cases. Performance benchmarks show up to 13x boost on new accelerators, roughly 56 tokens per second on iOS, and up to 35x faster runtime versus Llama on mobile. A robot demo on Raspberry Pi running LiteRT LLM on CPU demonstrates IoT inference. A new CLI tool with Python bindings is available for simplified deployment. Q&A confirms on-device face unlock uses similar frameworks, and open-weight models beyond Gemma are supported with proper conversion.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Edge Benefits
sections.summary: Chintan Parekh introduces himself as PM for LiteRT at Google AI Edge and outlines the agenda: new models, edge use cases, gallery app capabilities, deployment stack, and cross-platform support. He reviews key edge benefits including latency for real-time camera/video use cases, privacy for sensitive document summarization, offline capability, and cost savings through hybrid edge-cloud approaches.

sections.title: Gemma 4 Edge Models and New Capabilities
sections.summary: Covers Gemma 4 E2B (1-2 GB RAM, suited for voice and summarization) and E4B (heavier, for laptops/IoT). New agent capabilities include built-in function calling for local API interaction, native structured JSON output built into model architecture, chain-of-thought thinking mode, and hardware-native cross-platform support. Models are Apache 2.0 licensed on Hugging Face. Gemma 3 family also available down to 270M parameters.

sections.title: Gallery App Demos and Use Cases
sections.summary: Demos the gallery app showcasing on-device agent skills: Wikipedia querying, mood and sleep tracking with reasoning over 7-day trends, photo-to-music pairing with image understanding, and animal vocal call sound generation with multi-app workflow. All run on device with user-selectable CPU/GPU/NPU acceleration. App provides sample code, supports custom skill creation, and is open source on GitHub.

sections.title: Community Resources and LiteRT Framework
sections.summary: Highlights GitHub repo for community-shared skills, QR codes for skill-building guidance, and open-source sample app. Introduces LiteRT as Google's on-device framework built on TensorFlow Lite, using the same TFLite model format. LiteRT has 100,000+ apps, billions of active users, and extensive daily inference invocations, establishing a trusted deployment foundation.

sections.title: Cross-Platform Architecture and Development Stack
sections.summary: Explains LiteRT's cross-platform support: Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, web, and IoT using the same TFLite model format. Accepts PyTorch and JAX models via conversion, not just TensorFlow Lite. Introduces LiteRT Torch as the bring-your-own-model conversion path, Model Explorer for graph inspection and mixed-precision quantization, and AI Edge Portal as a cloud-based benchmarking service for testing deployability across device fleets including older phones. Covers AOT vs JIT compilation decisions.

sections.title: Hardware Acceleration and Performance
sections.summary: Details CPU and GPU as universal acceleration libraries. NPU integration complete with Qualcomm and MediaTek, with additional partner integrations underway. NPU delivers 3-10x improvement for real-time AR/VR and TTS use cases. Performance numbers include up to 13x boost on new accelerators, ~56 tokens/sec on iOS, and up to 35x faster runtime versus Llama on mobile. Desktop performance at par with Llama; IoT shows 3x improvement. Performance details available on Hugging Face model pages.

sections.title: Platform Coverage and Robot Demo
sections.summary: Shows Gemma model coverage tested across Android, iOS, Linux, and Raspberry Pi. Demos a robot built same morning running on Raspberry Pi with LiteRT LLM on CPU, responding to a visual sign by wiggling its antenna. Mentions a new CLI tool with Python bindings available on the website for simplified deployment.

sections.title: Q&A Session
sections.summary: Audience questions cover on-device face unlock (already running locally using similar frameworks on Google and Apple devices), home camera deployment (possible but requires different architecture for authenticity checking), Jetson Orin support (check Hugging Face), distributed agent architectures for local/remote orchestration, and support for open-weight models beyond Gemma (available with proper format conversion).
